Forecast Discussion

A cold front passes through from the NW during the evening. It's the leading edge of much cooler air. As energy to our north moves eastward, widely scattered evening showers and thundershowers are expected, mostly from Avery County northward; then a few stray showers remain possible along the west side of the Appalachians even after midnight.

We will be in a breezy, cool NW flow through Sunday. We will have a hint of fall in the air. That's not unusual for late August, but the duration of the trough over the Eastern U.S. this week is. Monday has pleasant but below-average temperatures. Tuesday is only slightly warmer as high pressure moves across the Central Appalachians and toward the Mid-Atlantic. Monday and Tuesday will make it hard to resist the call of the outdoors. Both days will be particularly cool in the valleys.

A frontal boundary to our south and east will edge northward Wednesday and Thursday. Temperatures return to seasonal levels, but moisture increases as well. Isolated afternoon and early evening showers and thundershowers are in play Wednesday.

A reinforcing front moves through the eastern trough Thursday, arriving here late in the day. We'll have more clouds with occasional showers and thundershowers Thursday that taper off during the evening.

Computer guidance differs on how quickly the front moves east. So we kept the mention of a stray shower or thundershower in the Friday forecast. Temperatures will remain near seasonal averages.
